pm.close: Father, your Son bound the strong man and gathered a new family around him. Keep us in that family by doing your will. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God answers Job out of the whirlwind and speaks of the sea he wrapped in swaddling bands and to which he set limits: thus far, and no farther.
In the storm on the lake Jesus sleeps, then rebukes the wind and says to the sea: Peace! Be still! The disciples ask: who then is this?
The love of Christ, who died for all, urges us on; whoever is in Christ is a new creation.
2027-06-20.action: Bring your present storm to Jesus in honest prayer, and pray for fishermen and seafarers.
2027-06-20.question: When the storm comes, do I trust that Jesus is in the boat with me?
catechism: What do the miracles of Jesus show?
Why did Christ die for all?
kidsaint: St Thomas More

Thomas More lived in England about five hundred years ago. He was a clever lawyer and the most important judge in the country, but at home he was a loving and cheerful father. He made sure his daughters studied just like his son, which was unusual in those days, and he wrote them letters full of love. When the king told everyone to deny the authority of the Pope over the Church in England, Thomas said no, because his conscience told him it was wrong. He was put in prison and then put to death, but he stayed calm and even joked kindly at the end. His feast is on Tuesday. Lesson: a good father, and a good child, stays calm in the storm because he trusts God.
2027-06-20.special: Twelfth Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). Father's Day in India and many countries.
term: The loving care with which God guides all his creation toward its goal, from the smallest things to the greatest events of history (Catechism 302–303). Providence does not mean that nothing bad will happen to us; it means that nothing happens outside God's care, and that he can bring good even out of storms (Romans 8:28).

family.explain: Jesus and his friends were in a boat when a big storm came. The waves were splashing into the boat, and the friends were very frightened. But Jesus was sleeping on a cushion! They woke him up, and he said to the wind and the sea: Peace! Be still! And everything became calm. When we are afraid, we can call Jesus too. He is always with us.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and their families during the monsoon, and for all fathers, especially those who live and work far from home.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes our family afraid? Let us give it to Jesus together.” Then let the children thank their father, or pray for him if he has died.

illus: An illustration

A fisherman from a coastal village near Kollam was out with four others in a small country boat when the monsoon wind turned suddenly. For two hours they bailed water with buckets and their bare hands. The youngest, a boy of nineteen on his first season, began to cry. The old helmsman, who had fished that coast for forty years, told him to keep bailing and say the Hail Mary with every bucket. When they reached the harbour mouth at last, the boy asked him whether he had not been afraid. The old man said: Of course I was afraid. But I have a picture of the Lord asleep in the boat stuck inside the cabin, and I know he does not sleep when we call him. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Master of the wind and the sea, you are in the boat with us. Calm the storms of our hearts and our homes, and increase our faith. Amen.
share: Thus far shall you come, and no farther (Job 38:11). Which storm in my life do I need to hear has a limit set by God?
Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? (Mark 4:38). When have I prayed like the disciples, and how did Jesus answer?
If anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17). What old thing in me does Christ want to make new?
pm.resp: Give thanks to the Lord, his love is everlasting.
interc: For the Church, the boat of Christ, that in every storm of history she may trust the Lord who is with her.
For fishermen, sailors and seafarers, especially those from our coasts, that they may be safe during the monsoon, and for their families waiting on shore.
For fathers, that they may be strong, gentle and faithful, and for fathers who have died.
For all who are passing through storms of illness, debt, conflict or grief, that they may hear the Lord say: Peace! Be still!
For our group, that the love of Christ may urge us on to live no longer for ourselves.
pm.close: Father, your Son stilled the wind and the waves with a word. Speak your peace into our lives, and bring us safely to the harbour of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Book of Wisdom teaches that God did not make death: he created us for incorruption, and death entered through the devil's envy.
St Paul asks the Corinthians to give generously, as Christ, though rich, became poor for our sakes, so that there may be a fair balance.
Jesus heals the woman who touches his cloak with faith and raises the daughter of Jairus: Do not fear, only believe. Talitha cum.
2027-06-27.action: Visit or call someone who is sick this week, and pray with them.
2027-06-27.question: Do I only press against Jesus in the crowd, or do I touch him with faith?
catechism: Why is Christ called the physician of souls and bodies?
Who may receive the Anointing of the Sick, and who celebrates it?
kidsaint: St Gianna Beretta Molla

Gianna was a doctor in Italy who loved children, mountains and skiing. She married Pietro and they had children whom she loved very much. When she was expecting her fourth baby, she became very ill. The doctors said that saving her own life might harm the baby. Gianna said: save the baby. Her daughter was born healthy in 1962, and a week later Gianna died. Pope John Paul II declared her a saint in 2004. Lesson: life is God's gift, and love is ready to give everything for another.
2027-06-27.special: Thirteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). Gloria and Creed. St Cyril of Alexandria omitted. Peter's Pence collection for the Holy Father's charity in many places (verify locally).
term: One of the seven sacraments. A priest anoints a seriously ill or elderly person, or one facing surgery, with blessed oil on the forehead and hands, praying that the Lord in his love and mercy will help them by the grace of the Holy Spirit and raise them up (James 5:14–15). It gives strength, peace and courage, forgives sins, and sometimes restores bodily health (Catechism 1499–1532). It is not only for the dying: ask for it in good time.

family.explain: A father named Jairus asked Jesus to come and heal his little girl. But on the way people said: it is too late, she has died. Jesus said to the father: do not be afraid, just believe. He went into the house, took the girl's hand and said: Talitha cum, little girl, get up! And she got up and walked! Jesus is stronger than sickness and even stronger than death.
family.intention: We pray for sick children and their parents, for doctors and nurses, and for families who have lost someone they love.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we know who is sick? Shall we pray for them together each evening this week, and visit them if we can?”

illus: An illustration

In a monsoon season some years ago, a fisherman from a village near Alappuzha sat for three nights outside the children's ward of a medical college hospital, where his nine-year-old daughter lay with severe dengue fever. Relatives kept phoning with stories of other children who had not survived. On the third night the hospital chaplain found him with a rosary and the Gospel of Mark open on his knee at chapter five. He said: Father, everyone tells me to prepare myself. I am only reading what Jesus said to the other father: do not fear, only believe. His daughter recovered. Not every story ends as Jairus' story did, and the chaplain knew it; but he said later that he had never seen the Gospel read with such faith. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Lord of life, you took the little girl by the hand. Take us by the hand now, and teach us to trust you. Amen.
share: God did not make death (Wisdom 1:13). How does this truth change the way I look at sickness, old age and death?
If I but touch his clothes, I will be made well (Mark 5:28). What do I need to bring to Jesus with the faith of this woman?
Do not fear, only believe (Mark 5:36). When have I been told it was too late, and how did God answer?
pm.resp: I will praise you, Lord, for you have rescued me.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be on the side of life, from conception to natural death.
For the Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV, and for the Peter's Pence collection, that it may relieve the poor and suffering in many lands.
For sick children, for their parents keeping watch, and for doctors and nurses, especially in this season of monsoon fevers.
For families who mourn a child or a young person, that they may hear the Lord's voice: do not fear.
For our group, that we may not only press around Jesus, but touch him with faith.
pm.close: Father, you created us for incorruption and in your Son you overcame death. Raise us up with him to new life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: King Herod kills James and imprisons Peter; while the Church prays fervently, an angel leads Peter out of prison.
Paul, near death in Rome, says: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith; the Lord stood by me.
Peter confesses Jesus as the Messiah, the Son of the living God; Jesus calls him the rock on which he will build his Church and gives him the keys of the kingdom.
2027-06-29.action: Pray today for Pope Leo XIV and for your bishop by name.
2027-06-29.question: Who is Jesus for me: an opinion I have heard, or the Son of the living God whom I confess?
catechism: What did Jesus give to Peter?
Why is the Pope the visible foundation of the Church's unity?
Why is the Church called apostolic?
kidsaint: Sts Peter and Paul

Peter was a fisherman with rough hands and a big heart. He sometimes spoke too fast and once even said he did not know Jesus. But Jesus forgave him and made him the leader of the apostles, the rock of the Church. Paul at first hated Christians, but Jesus met him on the road to Damascus, and he became the greatest missionary, travelling by land and sea to tell everyone about Jesus. Both of them died for Jesus in Rome. Lesson: Jesus can use anyone who loves him, even people who have made big mistakes.
2027-06-29.special: Solemnity of Sts Peter and Paul, Apostles. Gloria and Creed. Mass during the Day (the Vigil Mass was celebrated yesterday evening). The Pope blesses the pallia for new metropolitan archbishops. Pray for Pope Leo XIV.
term: A narrow circular band of white lamb's wool with six black crosses, worn over the chasuble around the shoulders. The Pope wears it, and so do metropolitan archbishops, as a sign of their authority as shepherds and of their communion with the successor of Peter. The wool recalls the lost sheep that the Good Shepherd carries on his shoulders. New archbishops receive the pallium blessed by the Pope on the solemnity of Sts Peter and Paul.

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do people say that I am? Then he asked: but who do you say that I am? Peter answered: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God! Jesus said: you are Peter, which means rock, and on this rock I will build my Church. Today the Pope, who lives in Rome, is the one who takes Peter's place, to keep the Church together. That is why we pray for him every day.
family.intention: We pray for Pope Leo XIV, for our bishop and our priests, and for Christians who are in prison or persecuted for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Can each of us say in our own words who Jesus is for us?” Then pray together one Our Father for the Pope.

illus: An illustration

During the monsoon fishing ban, when the big boats stay ashore, an old fisherman in a coastal parish near Thiruvananthapuram spends his mornings mending nets in the shade beside the church of St Peter. His name, like many on that coast, is Pathrose. A seminarian home for the holidays once asked him why he always ended his rosary with a prayer for the Pope. He said: my patron was a fisherman who sometimes sank in the water and sometimes ran away. Jesus still made him the rock. If Jesus could hold Peter up, he can hold up the Pope, and he can hold me up too. But the Pope has the heaviest net in the world to mend, so I help him with my beads. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you built your Church on the rock of Peter and sent Paul to the nations. Make us firm in the faith of the apostles. Amen.
share: But who do you say that I am? (Matthew 16:15). How would I answer Jesus today, in my own words?
While Peter was kept in prison, the church prayed fervently to God for him (Acts 12:5). For which imprisoned or suffering person or Church is God asking me to pray fervently?
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith (2 Timothy 4:7). Where do I need courage not to give up?
pm.resp: The angel of the Lord will rescue those who fear him.
interc: For Pope Leo XIV, successor of Peter, that the Lord may strengthen him to confirm his brothers in faith and to keep the Church in unity.
For the new metropolitan archbishops who receive the pallium, and for our own bishop.
For Christians imprisoned or persecuted for their faith, that the Church may pray for them as she prayed for Peter.
For missionaries, especially in India and Asia, that like Paul they may proclaim the word fully so that all nations may hear it.
For unity among all Christians, that the Churches may one day share the one table of the Lord.
pm.close: Father, you gave us the apostles Peter and Paul as our fathers in faith. Keep us in their teaching and bring us to share their crown. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ezekiel: God himself will take a tender sprig from the top of the cedar and plant it on a high mountain, where it will become a noble cedar sheltering every kind of bird.
Paul: we walk by faith, not by sight; we make it our aim to please the Lord, for all of us must appear before the judgment seat of Christ.
Jesus: the kingdom of God is like seed that grows by itself while the farmer sleeps, and like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, that becomes the greatest of shrubs.
2027-06-13.action: Sow one small seed of faith this week, a kind word, an invitation or a prayer, and leave the growth to God.
2027-06-13.question: Do I trust God with the slow, hidden growth of his kingdom in me and in those I love?
catechism: The Church, seed and beginning of the kingdom.
kidsaint: St Thérèse of Lisieux and the little way

St Thérèse lived in France about a hundred and thirty years ago and died when she was only twenty-four. She never did anything famous. She smiled at a sister who annoyed her, she did small jobs with love, and she offered everything to Jesus. She called this her “little way.” Today she is a Doctor of the Church and patron of the missions! Her small seeds of love grew into a great tree. Lesson: Jesus can make big things grow from the small good things you do every day.
2027-06-13.special: Eleventh Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year B: Gloria and Creed. St Antony of Padua is omitted because the date falls on a Sunday. Liturgical colour: green.
term: From the Greek parabolē, “a placing side by side.” A parable puts an ordinary thing (a seed, a lamp, a lost coin) beside the mystery of God's kingdom, so that the listener must think, choose and act. Jesus used parables to invite people in, not to give them a lecture.

family.explain: A farmer plants seeds and goes to sleep. He wakes up, he sleeps again, and the seeds grow all by themselves. He does not know how! Jesus says God's kingdom grows like that: quietly, even when we cannot see it. A mustard seed is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice, but it grows into a big plant where birds build their nests. When we do small good things with love, God makes them grow.
family.intention: We pray for farmers who are sowing in the monsoon rains, for children starting a new school year, and for the elderly, that they may stay green and fruitful.
family.ask: Ask: “What small seed of goodness can each of us plant this week?” Then plant a real seed in a pot together and watch it grow.

illus: An illustration

A retired teacher in a village near Thrissur used to keep a small notebook of the names of her former pupils. Every evening she prayed for five of them. Most of them she never saw again. Years after her death, one of them, now a priest in a mission in Madhya Pradesh, came to the parish to celebrate Mass for her. He told the people that when he was a frightened boy of twelve she had once stayed after class to help him with his lessons, and had said: I will pray for you every week. He had not thought of it for years, but it was that small seed, he said, that God had made grow. The teacher never knew. The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, it is good to give thanks to you, to declare your steadfast love in the morning and your faithfulness by night. Sow your word in our hearts and make it grow. Amen.
share: I myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of a cedar (Ezekiel 17:22). Where has God planted something new in my life when everything seemed broken?
The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how (Mark 4:27). What growth am I impatient for, in myself or in someone I love?
We walk by faith, not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7). Where am I being asked to trust what I cannot see?
pm.resp: Lord, it is good to give thanks to you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a mustard tree in whose shade the nations find a home.
For farmers sowing with the monsoon, and for those whose fields and houses suffer from floods and landslides.
For children and teachers beginning the new school year, that knowledge and faith may grow together in them.
For the elderly, that in old age they may still bear fruit and be honoured among us.
For all who honour St Antony of Padua, that like him they may love the poor and the word of God.
For our group, that we may sow patiently and leave the growth to God.
pm.close: Father, you give the growth to every seed sown in faith. Make your kingdom grow in us, quietly and surely, until the harvest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Tobit, a good man, is blinded by an accident and, humiliated, becomes suspicious of his wife Anna, who rebukes him: Where are your acts of charity?
Jesus answers the trap about taxes: Give to the emperor what is the emperor's, and to God what is God's; the coin bears Caesar's image, we bear God's.
St Justin, philosopher and martyr, paid his taxes but would not worship the gods; he was beheaded in Rome about 165.
2027-06-01.action: Do one act of trust and kindness at home today, where it is hardest.
2027-06-01.question: Do the people in my own house see the goodness that others see in me outside?
kidsaint: St Justin

Justin grew up in a family that did not know Jesus. He loved to ask big questions: who is God? why are we here? He went from teacher to teacher looking for answers. One day an old man by the sea told him to read the prophets of the Bible, and there Justin found Jesus, who is the Truth. Justin became a Christian teacher in Rome. When the judge told him to worship false gods, Justin said no, and he died as a martyr. Lesson: keep asking questions, and look for the answers in Jesus and his Word.

family.explain: Some men tried to trick Jesus with a question about money. Jesus asked for a coin and said: whose face is on it? The emperor's. Then give the emperor his coin. But give God what belongs to God. We do not have the emperor's face on us; we are made in God's image. So we belong to God: our hearts, our hands, our time.
family.intention: We pray for people who have lost their sight, and for families where there is suspicion and quarrelling.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we can give to God this week as a family, because we belong to him?”

illus: An illustration

A teacher in a Thrissur school once held up a ten-rupee note in a class of thirteen-year-olds and asked: whose picture is this? Gandhiji's, they said. And who owns the note? Whoever has it in his pocket, said one boy. Then she held up a small mirror and passed it round. Whose picture is this? Each child saw his own face. She said: the note goes to whoever has it; but your face is the image of God, and you belong to him wherever you go. One of those children, now a priest, says he still remembers that mirror. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you showed us the coin and the image. We give you ourselves, for we are made in your image. Open our eyes as you opened Tobit's. Amen.
share: Where are your acts of charity? (Tobit 2:14). Has suffering ever made me harsh or suspicious towards the people I love?
Their hearts are firm, secure in the Lord (Psalm 112:7). What bad news am I afraid of, and can I trust it to God?
Give to God the things that are God's (Mark 12:17). What in my life have I kept back from God?
pm.resp: Their hearts are firm, secure in the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that like St Justin she may meet every honest search for truth with patience and courage.
For rulers and governments, that they may serve the common good and respect the conscience of believers.
For the blind and those losing their sight, and for those who care for them.
For families where illness or poverty has brought quarrels and suspicion, that trust may be restored.
For students and teachers of philosophy, through the prayers of St Justin.
pm.close: Father, you made us in your image and redeemed us in your Son. Keep us loyal citizens and faithful children, giving to you what is yours. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: On the same day blind Tobit in Nineveh and grieving Sarah in Ecbatana pray to God, both asking to die.
At that very moment their prayers were heard in the glorious presence of God, and Raphael was sent to heal them both.
Jesus answers the Sadducees: in the resurrection we are like angels, and God is God not of the dead, but of the living.
2027-06-02.action: Pray today, by name, for someone in your family who has died.
2027-06-02.question: When I am at my lowest, do I stop praying, or do I pray more honestly?
kidsaint: Sts Marcellinus and Peter

Marcellinus was a priest and Peter helped him in the Church of Rome, long ago, when Christians were put in prison for loving Jesus. Even in prison they cheered up the other prisoners and told them about Jesus. They were put to death in a dark forest. But the man who killed them later became a Christian, and he told their story to a little boy, who grew up to be Pope Damasus. Today their names are still said at Mass. Lesson: when you are brave for Jesus, your story can help others believe.

family.explain: Tobit was blind and very sad. Far away, a young woman called Sarah was also very sad. On the same day, both of them prayed to God. And God heard both prayers at the same moment! He sent the angel Raphael to help them. God hears every prayer we pray, even when we are crying.
family.intention: We pray for people who are very sad today, and for our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we remember a time when God answered our family's prayer?”

illus: An illustration

A young nurse in a Kottayam hospital once told her parish priest that on the same evening two patients on her ward had asked her to pray that they might die: an old man in pain and a young widow after an accident. She prayed for both, not knowing what to ask. Months later she met them both again, by chance, at a parish retreat. The old man had found peace with his estranged son; the widow was helping in the parish kitchen. Neither had got the prayer they asked for. Both, she said, had received an answer. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, to you we lift up our souls. Hear the prayers we bring tonight, spoken and unspoken, and teach us your paths. Amen.
share: For it is better for me to die than to live (Tobit 3:6). Have I ever felt like Tobit or Sarah? Who helped me then?
At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard (Tobit 3:16). Do I believe God hears me even when I see no answer yet?
He is God not of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). How does faith in the resurrection change the way I grieve?
pm.resp: To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim with joy the resurrection of the dead.
For all who are tempted to despair or to take their own life, that someone may come to them as Raphael came.
For those who are mocked or shamed, like Sarah, especially women blamed for what is not their fault.
For our beloved dead, that the God of the living may bring them into his presence.
For priests and all who minister in prisons, through the prayers of Sts Marcellinus and Peter.
pm.close: Father, you heard Tobit and Sarah at the very moment they prayed. Hear us too, and lead us to the life that has no end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Tobias marries Sarah, and on their wedding night they first pray together: Grant that she and I may find mercy and that we may grow old together.
Jesus names the first commandment, to love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength, and the second, to love your neighbour as yourself; a scribe is told he is not far from the kingdom.
St Charles Lwanga and his young companions in Uganda kept their faith and purity and were burned at Namugongo on 3 June 1886.
2027-06-03.action: Pray tonight for married couples, and offer God one part of yourself that you have held back.
2027-06-03.question: Do I love God with all my heart, soul, mind and strength, or only with what is left over?
kidsaint: St Kizito

Kizito was a boy in Uganda, only about fourteen, who served in the king's palace. He learned about Jesus from Charles Lwanga, the leader of the palace boys, and he wanted very much to be baptised. When the king began to kill Christians, Kizito was baptised by Charles the night before they were arrested. On the way to death he held Charles's hand and was not afraid. Lesson: even a young person can be very brave for Jesus, and a good friend helps you stay faithful.

family.explain: Tobias and Sarah got married. On their wedding night, before anything else, they knelt down together and prayed. They thanked God for making husband and wife, and they asked him to let them grow old together. Families that pray together are strong. Jesus also said that the greatest commandment is to love God with all our heart and to love our neighbour as ourselves.
family.intention: We pray for our parents and grandparents, for all married couples, and for young people who must be brave for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When can our family pray together every day this week?”

illus: An illustration

A couple in Kollam celebrating their fiftieth wedding anniversary were asked by their grandchildren what their secret was. The grandmother smiled and said that on their wedding night, before anything else, her husband had asked her to kneel with him and pray the Our Father. Then, she said, we did it again the next night, and the next, for fifty years. On the nights we were angry with each other, it was hard to start, but we never ended the day without it. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, our God, you are one Lord. We want to love you with all our heart, soul, mind and strength, and to love one another as ourselves. Be among us now. Amen.
share: Sister, get up, and let us pray (Tobit 8:4). How much does prayer shape my family life?
Not because of lust, but with sincerity (Tobit 8:7). How can I help the young people I know to love purely?
You are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). What still keeps me from loving God with my whole self?
pm.resp: Happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways.
interc: For married couples, that like Tobias and Sarah they may begin and end each day in prayer.
For young men and women preparing for marriage, that they may love with sincerity and purity.
For the Church in Uganda and in all Africa, that the seed of the martyrs may bear abundant fruit.
For young people who are pressured to do wrong by those in power, that they may have the courage of the Uganda martyrs.
For Christians of every Church who suffer for Christ, and for unity among all who confess his name.
pm.close: Father, the martyrs of Uganda loved you more than life. Give us their courage and their purity, and keep our homes in your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Through Hosea God speaks as a parent who taught his child to walk; when Israel turns away, his heart recoils and his compassion grows warm and tender.
Paul prays that Christ may dwell in our hearts and that we may know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.
On the Cross a soldier pierces the side of Jesus and blood and water flow out: the Lamb whose bones are not broken, the source of the sacraments and of the Church.
2027-06-04.action: Gather your family before an image of the Sacred Heart tonight and renew your consecration; pray for your priests.
2027-06-04.question: Do I think of God's heart as angry with me, or as Hosea shows it, recoiling from anger and burning with compassion?
catechism: The Sacred Heart: Jesus loved each of us with a human heart.
The Church born from the pierced side of Christ.
Prayer to the Heart of Jesus.
kidsaint: St Margaret Mary Alacoque

Margaret Mary was a girl in France who was often sick and lonely, and she found her best friend in Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. She became a sister in a convent. Jesus showed her his Heart, full of love like a fire, and asked her to tell everyone how much he loves them. Many people did not believe her at first, but she kept praying and loving. Because of her we have the feast of the Sacred Heart and the First Fridays. Lesson: Jesus' heart is full of love for you; give him your love in return.
2027-06-04.special: Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus (Year B). Gloria and Creed. World Day of Prayer for the Sanctification of Priests. First Friday of June, the month of the Sacred Heart.
term: Love offered to make up for the coldness, ingratitude and sins by which the love of Christ is wounded. In devotion to the Sacred Heart, reparation means consoling the Lord by our love, especially through Holy Communion received on the First Fridays and the Holy Hour, and repairing the harm of sin by works of justice and charity (Pius XI, Miserentissimus Redemptor, 1928; Pope Francis, Dilexit Nos).

family.explain: God says: I taught you to walk, I held you in my arms, I lifted you to my cheek, I bent down and fed you. That is how much God loves us! And Jesus showed us God's love with his own heart. On the Cross his heart was pierced for us. When we look at the picture of the Sacred Heart in our home, we remember: Jesus loves me with a real human heart, and with all the love of God.
family.intention: We pray for all the priests who have served our family, and for children who are learning to walk and talk.
family.ask: Ask: “Where is the Sacred Heart picture in our home, and how can we pray before it together this month?”

illus: An illustration

In a hill-country parish in Idukki, an old rubber tapper had kept a lamp burning before a faded picture of the Sacred Heart in his small house for forty years. When the monsoon floods took his house, he lost almost everything. The parish found him a new room, and the first thing he asked for was not a cot but a nail on the wall. A neighbour brought him a new picture. He hung it, lit a small lamp, and said: now this is home. Love that is seen, he said, keeps the heart warm when everything else is wet. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, we gather before you. Draw us with the cords of human kindness, with bands of love, and teach us to drink with joy from the wells of salvation. Amen.
share: I was to them like those who lift infants to their cheeks (Hosea 11:4). When have I felt God hold me like a child?
To know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge (Ephesians 3:19). How do I come to know Christ's love: in prayer, in the sacraments, in people?
At once blood and water came out (John 19:34). What does the pierced Heart of Jesus ask of me this month?
pm.resp: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
interc: For the Church, born from the pierced side of Christ, that she may always proclaim his merciful love.
For priests, on this World Day of Prayer for their sanctification, that they may be men after the Heart of Jesus.
For families consecrated to the Sacred Heart, that their homes may be places of mercy and peace.
For those who feel unloved or have turned away from God, that they may be drawn back with bands of love.
For the sick and dying, that they may rest in the Heart of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, in the Heart of your Son you have shown us the depth of your love. Make our hearts like his, gentle and humble. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Isaiah sings of Zion clothed in salvation like a bride, and Hannah of the God who lifts the lowly: the Church hears in both the voice of Mary.
Mary and Joseph search for the twelve-year-old Jesus for three days and find him in his Father's house; they do not understand, but his mother treasured all these things in her heart.
St Boniface, apostle of Germany, was martyred at Dokkum on 5 June 754; the weekday Gospel praises the widow who gave all she had.
2027-06-05.action: Renew your consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary today, and carry one word of the Gospel in your heart all day.
2027-06-05.question: When I do not understand what God is doing, do I keep and ponder, or do I complain and walk away?
catechism: The finding of Jesus in the Temple.
Jesus learns to pray from the heart of his mother.
Mary, full of grace, preserved from all stain of sin.
kidsaint: St Boniface

Boniface was a monk from England who went to Germany to tell people about Jesus. Many people there worshipped a huge old oak tree, thinking a god called Thor lived in it. Boniface took an axe and cut the tree down! Nothing bad happened to him, and the people saw that the true God is stronger. He used the wood to build a little chapel. When he was very old, he was killed by robbers while he was getting ready to confirm new Christians. Lesson: be brave to show people that Jesus is the true God.
2027-06-05.special: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary and St Boniface, bishop and martyr: two obligatory memorials falling on the same day, so both optional in 2027 (follow the diocesan Ordo). World Environment Day.
term: The heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary, never touched by sin, because she was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception by the grace of God in view of the merits of Christ (Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus, 1854). In devotion the “heart” means the whole inner person: her faith, love, sorrow and contemplation. To honour her Immaculate Heart is to honour her love for God and for us, and to learn from her how to keep the Word of God.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he stayed in the Temple in Jerusalem, and Mary and Joseph searched for him for three days. When they found him, Jesus said that he had to be in his Father's house. Mary did not understand everything, but she kept it all in her heart and thought about it. Our Mother Mary's heart is full of love for Jesus and for us. She can help us when we feel lost.
family.intention: We pray for children who are lost or separated from their families, and for parents who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing about Jesus we want to keep in our hearts this week, like Mary did?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Thiruvananthapuram kept a small notebook on her kitchen shelf. In it she wrote, over twenty years, things her children said about God: a question at bedtime, a prayer one of them made up, the day her son said he wanted to be a priest and the day he said he did not. When that son, grown up, was going through a dark time, she gave him the notebook. He read it in one night and came home the next Sunday. She said she had learned it from the Gospel: his mother treasured all these things in her heart. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, your Heart kept every word of your Son. Gather us around Jesus as you gathered the apostles, and teach us to keep his word. Amen.
share: He has clothed me with the garments of salvation (Isaiah 61:10). What does it mean for me that God has clothed me with salvation in Baptism?
Your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety (Luke 2:48). When have I lost Jesus, and how did I find him again?
His mother treasured all these things in her heart (Luke 2:51). What word of God am I treasuring at this time of my life?
pm.resp: My heart exults in the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may keep the Word of God and ponder it in her heart.
For the world, consecrated to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, that peace may come where there is war.
For parents searching for children who have wandered away from God or from home.
For missionaries, through the prayers of St Boniface, that they may preach with courage.
For the care of creation on World Environment Day, that we may tend the earth as God's garden.
pm.close: Father, you gave Mary a heart that was wholly yours. Through her prayers, give us hearts that search for your Son, keep his word, and give him everything. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul begins his most personal letter by blessing the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who comforts us in every affliction.
The comfort we receive from God is meant to flow on to others who suffer.
Jesus opens the Sermon on the Mount with the Beatitudes: the poor in spirit, the mourners, the meek and the merciful are blessed.
2027-06-07.action: Visit, call or message one person who is suffering today, and bring them a little of the comfort God has given you.
2027-06-07.question: Which Beatitude do I most need to grow into, and which do I most resist?

family.explain: Jesus went up a mountain and sat down to teach. He told his friends who are the really happy people in God's eyes: not the people who have the most toys or money, but people who are humble, kind, gentle, who make peace and who have clean hearts. St Paul says God comforts us when we are sad, so that we can comfort others.
family.intention: We pray for children and teachers starting the new school year, and for families who are sad or in trouble.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of Jesus' blessings can each of us live at school or at work this week?”

illus: An illustration

On the first day of school in a town in Kottayam, a boy in the third standard stood crying at the gate because his father had died during the vacation and he did not want to go in. An older girl, who had lost her own mother two years before, left her friends, took his hand and said: I know; I cried too; come, sit with me today. She walked him to his class and came back at the lunch break. Their teacher said later that the girl had done what no adult could have done, because she knew from the inside what he felt. She had been comforted, and she passed the comfort on. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Father of mercies, God of all consolation, comfort us in our troubles and make us comforters of others. Teach us the happiness of the Beatitudes. Amen.
share: God consoles us in all our affliction so that we may console others (2 Corinthians 1:4). When did God comfort me, and whom could I comfort with that same comfort?
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted (Matthew 5:4). Is there a grief in my life that I have not yet brought to Jesus?
Blessed are the poor in spirit (Matthew 5:3). What does it mean for me to be poor in spirit at home or at work?
pm.resp: Taste and see the goodness of the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of comfort for all who are afflicted.
For those who mourn the death of someone they love, that they may be comforted.
For children, students and teachers beginning a new school year, and for safety during the monsoon rains.
For Christians persecuted for righteousness' sake, that they may know the reward Jesus promised.
For our group, that we may comfort one another as God comforts us.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you are the meek and humble of heart. Make our hearts like yours, and lead us to the kingdom promised to the poor in spirit. Amen.

quick: Paul's travel plans changed, but God's word does not: in Jesus Christ every promise of God is a Yes, and through him we say Amen.
God has anointed us, put his seal on us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a first installment, words the Church reads of Baptism and Confirmation.
Jesus tells his disciples: you are the salt of the earth and the light of the world; let your light shine so that others give glory to the Father.
2027-06-08.action: Keep one promise today that you have been postponing, and keep it fully.
2027-06-08.question: Is my light on the lampstand, or have I hidden it under a basket out of fear or laziness?

family.explain: Jesus said to his friends: you are salt and you are light. Salt makes food tasty and keeps it from spoiling. Light helps people see. Christians are meant to make the world better and to help people see God. When we do good things, people should not say: how good they are! but: how good God is!
family.intention: We pray for families without electricity or shelter during the heavy rains, and for all who keep their promises when it is hard.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is a light for our family? How can each of us be a little lamp at home this week?”

illus: An illustration

During a heavy monsoon night in a village near Thrissur, the power failed and the whole lane went dark. In one house a grandmother, who had lit the nilavilakku every evening for sixty years, simply brought the lamp from the prayer corner and set it on the table in the front room, with the door open. Neighbours who were stumbling about with torches whose batteries were dying came and sat on her veranda. Someone started a hymn; somebody else brought tea. Her grandson remembered later that nobody talked about the grandmother that night; they talked about how good it was to be together and to pray. The lamp was not hidden, and the glory went to God. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Faithful God, your Yes in Christ never changes. Seal us again with your Spirit and make us salt and light for the people around us. Amen.
share: In him every one of God's promises is a Yes (2 Corinthians 1:20). Which promise of God do I most need to trust today?
God has put his seal on us and given us his Spirit (2 Corinthians 1:22). Do I live as someone sealed and anointed by God?
You are the light of the world (Matthew 5:14). Where is my light hidden, at home, at work or in my parish?
pm.resp: Lord, let your face shine on me.
interc: For the Church, that her members may be salt and light in a world that has lost its taste for God.
For all who were confirmed this year, that they may live by the Spirit they received.
For people living in darkness, sadness or despair, that they may see the light of Christ in us.
For families affected by the monsoon rains, for safety and for help from their neighbours.
For our group, that our yes may be yes and our promises kept.
pm.close: Father, may our good works shine before others so that they may give glory to you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul says the Corinthians are his letter, written by the Spirit on human hearts; his competence as a minister comes from God.
The Law of Sinai came in glory and is holy, but the letter alone cannot give life; the Spirit writes God's will within us.
Jesus came not to abolish the law and the prophets but to fulfill them; St Ephrem, the Harp of the Spirit, sang this faith in his hymns.
2027-06-09.action: Pray slowly through the Ten Commandments tonight, and thank Jesus for one that he has helped you to keep from the heart.
2027-06-09.question: Do I keep God's commandments only because I must, or because I have come to love them?
kidsaint: St Ephrem the Syrian

Ephrem lived about 1,700 years ago in a city called Nisibis, near the border of the Roman Empire. He was a deacon, which means a helper of the bishop. He loved God so much that he wrote hundreds of hymns, poems you can sing, about Jesus, Mary, the Bible and the sacraments. He taught choirs of women and girls to sing them in church, so that everybody could learn the faith by heart. People called him the Harp of the Holy Spirit. At the end of his life, when there was a famine, he worked hard to bring food to the hungry. Lesson: you can praise God with your voice and your songs, and you can help others learn about Jesus through music.

family.explain: Jesus said: I did not come to throw away God's commandments, but to fulfill them, to show their full meaning. God's commandments are like a fence that keeps us safe. Jesus teaches us to keep them not because we are afraid, but because we love God and love our neighbours. The Holy Spirit writes God's law in our hearts.
family.intention: We pray for all who teach the faith: parents, catechists and Sunday-school teachers, and for church choirs.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of the Ten Commandments is hardest for our family? How can we help one another keep it with love?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a parish near Kollam found her Class Six students bored by the Ten Commandments. One Sunday she brought a mango sapling tied to a stick. She said: this stick is like the Law; it keeps the young tree straight while it is weak. But the life is not in the stick; the life is in the sap that rises from the roots. The Holy Spirit is the sap. When the tree is grown strong, it stands straight by itself, but it has not thrown away what the stick taught it. A boy said: so Jesus did not throw away the stick; he gave the tree its life. She said that was the best summary of Matthew 5:17 she had ever heard. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Holy Spirit, Lord and giver of life, write God's law on our hearts. Make us letters of Christ that all can read. Amen.
share: You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts (2 Corinthians 3:2). If people read my life as a letter of Christ, what would they read?
The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). Is my faith a matter of outward rules only, or is it alive in the Spirit?
I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). How does Jesus show me the full meaning of a commandment I find hard?
pm.resp: Holy is the Lord our God.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a minister of the new covenant, full of the Spirit who gives life.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in love of his name and in faithfulness to his covenant.
For all who teach and sing the faith, through the prayers of St Ephrem, especially catechists and church choirs.
For the Syriac Churches of Kerala and the Middle East, who honour Mar Aprem, and for Christians in the lands where he lived.
For our group, that the Spirit may write the commandments of God on our hearts.
pm.close: God of the covenant, you gave your Law in glory and your Spirit in greater glory. Make us faithful in the smallest things and generous in the greatest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: When anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is removed from the heart, and the Scriptures reveal Christ.
With unveiled faces, Christians are being transformed from glory to glory into the image of Christ, in whose face God's light shines.
Jesus goes to the root of the commandment against murder: anger and insult; he asks us to be reconciled before offering our gift at the altar.
2027-06-10.action: Take one concrete step today towards reconciliation with someone you are at odds with.
2027-06-10.question: Is there someone whose name I would not want to hear at the sign of peace?

family.explain: Jesus said: if you are going to church to give a gift to God, and you remember that someone is angry with you, first go and make peace with that person, and then come back and give your gift. God does not want us to pray with one hand and fight with the other. Making peace makes our faces shine with God's light.
family.intention: We pray for families where there are quarrels, and for peace between neighbours, between religions and between nations.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone our family needs to make peace with? What small step can we take this week?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village in Wayanad had not spoken for six years over a boundary of a few cents of land. Every Sunday they sat in the same church, on opposite sides. One year the younger brother heard this Gospel read on a weekday and could not get it out of his mind. On the following Sunday, as the people stood to exchange the sign of peace, he crossed the aisle and held out his hand. The older brother hesitated, then embraced him, and both of them wept. The parish priest said later that he had preached on reconciliation many times, but that morning the whole church saw it. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, take away the veil from our hearts and let your face shine on us. Give us the grace to forgive and to be reconciled. Amen.
share: When one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed (2 Corinthians 3:16). Is there a part of God's word I read without really seeing Christ in it?
We are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another (2 Corinthians 3:18). In what way has Christ been changing me this year?
First be reconciled to your brother or sister (Matthew 5:24). Whom do I need to be reconciled with before I next go to the altar?
pm.resp: The glory of the Lord will dwell in our land.
interc: For the Church, that she may reflect the glory of Christ with an unveiled face.
For the Jewish people, that God may bless them in their faithfulness to his covenant, and for growing friendship between Jews and Christians.
For families and neighbours divided by quarrels over land, money or words, that they may be reconciled.
For our country and our land, that righteousness and peace may embrace, and for good rain and safety in the monsoon.
For our group, that we may never bring a gift to God while refusing peace to a brother or sister.
pm.close: Father, you shone in our hearts in the face of Jesus Christ. Make us bearers of his light and his peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Barnabas, the son of encouragement, saw the grace of God at Antioch and rejoiced; he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.
He went to Tarsus to bring Saul to Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians; later the Spirit set the two apart for mission.
Jesus sends his apostles to proclaim the kingdom, heal and bring peace: you received without payment; give without payment.
2027-06-11.action: Write or say a word of encouragement today to someone who is new, struggling or has failed.
2027-06-11.question: Do I see the grace of God in others and rejoice, or do I look first for their faults?
kidsaint: St Barnabas

Barnabas was a kind man from the island of Cyprus. His real name was Joseph, but the apostles called him Barnabas, which means son of encouragement, because he always cheered people up. When Saul, who used to hurt Christians, became a follower of Jesus, everybody was afraid of him. But Barnabas took him by the hand and said: he has really changed; give him a chance. Saul became the great St Paul! Later Barnabas also gave a young man called Mark a second chance, and Mark wrote one of the four Gospels. Lesson: be an encourager; a kind word can help someone become a saint.

family.explain: The Church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to the city of Antioch to see what was happening there. He saw that many people had come to believe in Jesus, and he was very happy. He encouraged them. Then he went to find his friend Saul to help him teach. In Antioch the followers of Jesus were first called Christians. That is our name too!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, for new Christians and for people who need someone to believe in them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family or class needs a word of encouragement this week? What will we say to them?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a parish in Ernakulam failed his final examinations and stopped coming to church because he was ashamed. Most people forgot him. One elderly member of the parish council, a retired schoolmaster, did not. Every week he stopped by the young man's house with a newspaper cutting about a course or a job, and every week he said: I am praying for you; you are not finished. The young man passed the next year, later trained as a nurse, and now works in a hospital in another state, where he organises the youth group of his parish. When he came home for Christmas he went straight to the old man's house first. The parish priest called the schoolmaster our Barnabas. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who set apart Barnabas and Saul for your work, fill us with faith and goodness, and make us encouragers of our brothers and sisters. Amen.
share: When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced (Acts 11:23). When I meet others, do I look first for the grace of God in them?
Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul (Acts 11:25). Is there someone whose gifts I should bring forward, even if they outshine mine?
You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). What have I received from God that I am keeping to myself?
pm.resp: The Lord has revealed to the nations his saving power.
interc: For the Church, that she may have many sons and daughters of encouragement who rejoice in the grace of God.
For missionaries, priests, religious and lay people, sent out from Kerala and India to other lands.
For new Christians and those returning to the faith, that they may find a Barnabas who welcomes them.
For the Church in Cyprus and in all the lands where Barnabas preached, and for peace in the Middle East.
For our group, that we may give second chances as Barnabas gave one to Mark.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you sent your apostles to proclaim that the kingdom has come near. Send us too, with your peace, into every home we enter. Amen.

quick: The love of Christ urges us on: one died for all, so that those who live may live no longer for themselves but for him.
If anyone is in Christ there is a new creation; God reconciled the world to himself in Christ and has made us ambassadors of reconciliation.
Jesus asks his disciples not to swear at all but to let their word be Yes, Yes or No, No; Mary's Yes is the model.
2027-06-12.action: Go to confession this weekend, or help someone else to go.
2027-06-12.question: Do people trust my word without my needing to swear or exaggerate?

family.explain: St Paul says that when we belong to Jesus, we become a new creation: the old is gone, the new has come! God wants to make friends with everyone again, through Jesus. That is what happens in confession: God forgives us and makes us new. Jesus also teaches us to always tell the truth, so that our yes means yes and our no means no.
family.intention: We pray for priests who hear confessions, and for people who are afraid to come back to God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we need to say sorry for in our family? Who will be the first to make peace?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Alappuzha had not been to confession for almost thirty years. Every Saturday evening she walked past the church on her way to the market and saw the short line near the confessional. One Saturday in the rain she stepped inside only to wait for the shower to pass. The priest was sitting there with no one in front of him. She told him later that she sat down intending to say only good evening, Father, and then everything came out. When she left, the rain had stopped and the road was shining. She said to her daughter: I felt like a new person. Her daughter, who knew 2 Corinthians 5:17 from school, said: Amma, you are a new creation. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your love urges us on. Make us new creatures, ambassadors of your reconciliation, and people whose word can be trusted. Amen.
share: The love of Christ urges us on (2 Corinthians 5:14). Does the love of Christ move me, or do I move only when others push me?
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17). What old thing in my life does Christ want to pass away?
Let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). Where do I bend the truth, exaggerate or make promises I do not keep?
pm.resp: The Lord is kind and merciful.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a faithful ambassador of the reconciliation God offers in Christ.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be patient, merciful and wise.
For those who have been away from the sacraments for many years, that they may come home and find a welcome.
For nations, communities and families torn apart, that they may be reconciled.
For our group, through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, that our yes may be like hers.
pm.close: Merciful Father, as far as the east is from the west, so far you remove our sins from us. Make us new in Christ, and send us out as his ambassadors. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive the grace of God in vain: now is the acceptable time, now is the day of salvation.
He describes his sufferings as a minister of Christ: sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing yet possessing everything.
Jesus replaces “an eye for an eye” with a new way: turn the other cheek, give your cloak as well, go the second mile.
2027-06-14.action: Answer one unkind word today with a kind one, or do more than you are asked for someone who demands your help.
2027-06-14.question: When I am wronged, do I keep the chain of revenge going, or do I break it with goodness?

family.explain: Long ago people said: if someone hurts you, you may hurt them back the same amount. Jesus says something new: do not hit back. If someone is unkind, be kind. If someone asks you to help, help even more than they ask. That is how we stop quarrels from growing. It is not easy, but Jesus helps us.
family.intention: We pray for children and teachers in the new school year, that classrooms may be places of kindness and not of bullying.
family.ask: Ask: “When someone in our family is unkind, how can we answer with kindness instead of anger?”

illus: An illustration

In a busy office in Kochi, a senior clerk was known for shouting at the younger staff. One morning he threw a file on the desk of a new employee and blamed her loudly for a mistake that was not hers. She said nothing. At lunch she noticed that he had not eaten; she knew he was diabetic and had heard that his wife was in hospital. She quietly placed a packet of food and a cup of tea on his desk. He looked at her for a long moment and said nothing. The next day he came to her desk and apologised, the first time anyone in that office had heard him do so. She had gone the second mile. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, you have done marvellous things. Make us witnesses of your love today, and break in us every chain of revenge. Amen.
share: See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! (2 Corinthians 6:2). What grace of God am I putting off for later?
As having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). What does it mean for me that Christ is my wealth?
If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Who is asking me for more than I want to give?
pm.resp: The Lord has made known his salvation.
interc: For priests, religious and missionaries, that like Paul they may serve with endurance and joy.
For those who suffer insults and injustice, that they may be strengthened and protected.
For victims of violence in their own homes, that they may find safety and help.
For students and teachers at the start of the new school year.
For our group, that we may answer evil with good.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to turn the other cheek and to go the second mile. Give us his heart, so that we may overcome evil with good. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul tells the Corinthians how the poor churches of Macedonia gave with joy, beyond their means, because they first gave themselves to the Lord.
The model of all giving is Christ, who though he was rich became poor for our sakes, so that by his poverty we might become rich.
Jesus commands: love your enemies, pray for your persecutors, and be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect.
2027-06-15.action: Pray by name today for someone who has hurt you, and ask God to bless them.
2027-06-15.question: Does my love stop at the edge of my own family and friends, or does it reach, like the rain, to those who do not love me?

family.explain: Look out of the window when it rains. The rain falls on every house, every field, every tree. It does not ask: is this a good person or a bad person? Jesus says God loves like that. He sends the sun and the rain on everyone. And he asks us to love like that too, even people who are not kind to us, and to pray for them.
family.intention: We pray for people who have hurt our family, and for families that are not speaking to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we find hard to love? Can we say a prayer for them together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

Sister Rani Maria Vattalil, a Franciscan Clarist sister from Kerala, worked among the poor in Madhya Pradesh. In 1995 she was stabbed to death on a bus by a man hired by those who resented her work. Years later her own sister, Sister Selmy Paul, visited the murderer, Samundar Singh, in prison and tied a rakhi on his wrist, the thread that makes him a brother. Her family forgave him, and he came to repent and was present at Sister Rani Maria's beatification in Indore in 2017. Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you. (A true story.)

pm.open: Praise the Lord, O my soul! You make your sun rise on the evil and on the good. Make our hearts as wide as yours. Amen.
share: They gave themselves first to the Lord (2 Corinthians 8:5). Have I given myself to the Lord, or only some of my things?
Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor (2 Corinthians 8:9). How has Christ made me rich?
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Whom do I need to pray for today?
pm.resp: Praise the Lord, my soul!
interc: For the poor, and for all who share generously with them out of their own little.
For those who persecute Christians in India and in the world, that their hearts may be changed.
For families and neighbours divided by old enmities.
For farmers waiting for the rain, and for those who suffer from floods.
For our group, that we may love as the Father loves.
pm.close: Father, your Son became poor to make us rich and taught us to love our enemies. Make us your children in deed and in truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: whoever sows bountifully will reap bountifully; give as you have decided in your heart, for God loves a cheerful giver.
God gives abundantly to the generous, so that they may share in every good work, and their giving becomes thanksgiving to God.
Jesus: give alms, pray and fast not to be seen by others but in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
2027-06-16.action: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about, except your Father in heaven.
2027-06-16.question: For whom do I really give, pray and fast: for God, or for the eyes of others?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you do something good, do not show off. When you share, do it quietly. When you pray, you can go into your room, close the door and talk to God alone. God sees everything, even the things nobody else sees, and he is happy with what we do for him with love.
family.intention: We pray for the poor in our neighbourhood, and for all who help them quietly.
family.ask: Ask: “What secret good deed can each of us do for someone in the family this week?” Then do it without telling!

illus: An illustration

For many years the poor families of a parish in Kollam found, every month, a sack of rice and some money left at the door of the parish office, with a note: for those who need it. Nobody knew who brought it. When an old fisherman of the parish died, his son found in his house a notebook with the dates and amounts carefully written down, every month for twenty-two years. The man had never been rich, and had never spoken of it to anyone, not even to his own family. At his funeral the parish priest read only one line from the Gospel: your Father who sees in secret will reward you. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Father, you love a cheerful giver and you see in secret. Give us generous and humble hearts. Amen.
share: The one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). Am I sowing sparingly or bountifully in my giving?
God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). Do I give with joy, or reluctantly?
Your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:4). What do I do only to be seen?
pm.resp: Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that her works of charity may be done with humility and joy.
For the poor and the hungry, and for all who share their bread in secret.
For those who are tempted to do good only for praise.
For all who pray and fast for others, hidden and unknown.
For our group, that our prayer may be true and our giving cheerful.
pm.close: Father, you see in secret and you reward the hidden gift. Make us cheerful givers and sincere in prayer. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul feels a divine jealousy for the Corinthians: he has promised them as a chaste virgin to Christ, and fears they may be led away to another Jesus or a different gospel.
He preached to them without asking for support, because he loves them.
Jesus warns against empty words in prayer, teaches the Our Father, and says that the Father forgives us as we forgive others.
2027-06-17.action: Pray the Our Father once today very slowly, and forgive someone at the words “as we also have forgiven.”
2027-06-17.question: When I pray the Our Father, do I mean the words, especially “your will be done” and “as we forgive”?

family.explain: Jesus' friends asked him: how should we pray? He taught them the prayer we call the Our Father. We do not need to use many words, because God already knows what we need. First we praise God and ask for his kingdom to come; then we ask for food, for forgiveness and for protection from evil. And Jesus says: if we want God to forgive us, we must forgive others.
family.intention: We pray for all who are learning to pray: little children, catechumens, and those who have forgotten how.
family.ask: Ask: “Which line of the Our Father is your favourite, and why?” Then pray it together holding hands.

illus: An illustration

A young mother in Bengaluru was teaching her four-year-old son the Our Father. When they came to “give us this day our daily bread,” the boy stopped and asked: why do we ask God for bread, when Appa buys it from the shop? The mother thought for a moment, then took him to the window. She showed him the rain falling on the trees, the vendor pushing his cart of vegetables, the bus driver taking his father to work. All of this, she said, is how God gives us bread. Appa works, but God gives him strength, and rain, and work to do. The boy prayed the line again, slowly, and added on his own: and give bread to that man too, pointing at a beggar on the corner. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Teach us to pray as children, with few words and full hearts. Amen.
share: I feel a divine jealousy for you (2 Corinthians 11:2). Is my heart undivided in its love for Christ?
Your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:8). Do I trust the Father with my needs?
If you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Whom do I need to forgive before I can pray the Our Father honestly?
pm.resp: Your works, O Lord, are justice and truth.
interc: For the Church, the bride of Christ, that she may remain faithful to the one Gospel.
For those who have no daily bread, and for those who share theirs.
For all who are tempted, that the Father may rescue them from the evil one.
For those who find it hard to pray, and for children learning the Our Father.
For our group, that we may pray with sincere hearts and forgive one another.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to call you Our Father. Hear the prayer we make in his words, and make us one family of forgiven and forgiving children. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul, speaking “as a fool,” lists not his successes but his sufferings: beatings, shipwrecks, dangers, hunger, and his daily anxiety for all the churches.
He concludes that if he must boast, he will boast of his weakness.
Jesus: store up treasures in heaven, not on earth, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be; the eye is the lamp of the body.
2027-06-18.action: Give away one thing you are attached to, or give one hour to someone in need.
2027-06-18.question: Where is my treasure, and so where is my heart?

family.explain: Jesus says: do not spend your life collecting things that get old, break or are stolen, like toys, phones and money. Collect treasures in heaven: kindness, prayer, sharing, forgiveness. Nobody can steal these! And he says: where your treasure is, your heart will be. If we love Jesus most, our heart will be with him.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and pastors who suffer for the Church, and for the poor who have no treasure on earth.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the most precious thing in our house? What is the most precious thing in heaven for us?”

illus: An illustration

An elderly widow in Changanassery kept a small steel box under her bed. When she died, her children opened it, expecting to find gold. Inside they found her wedding ring, a rosary worn smooth, a bundle of letters, and a list in her handwriting: the names of every poor child whose school fees she had paid over forty years, with the year each one finished school. There were sixty-three names. Her grandson, a young engineer, read the list twice and then said quietly: so this is where her heart was. Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, from all their afflictions you deliver the just. Draw our hearts to the treasure that does not pass away. Amen.
share: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness (2 Corinthians 11:30). Can I accept my weakness as a place for Christ's power?
I am under daily pressure because of my anxiety for all the churches (2 Corinthians 11:28). Do I carry the Church in my prayer?
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Matthew 6:21). What does my use of time and money say about my heart?
pm.resp: From all their afflictions God will deliver the just.
interc: For the Pope, bishops and priests, who carry the daily care of all the churches.
For missionaries and Christians who suffer hunger, danger and persecution for the Gospel.
For those enslaved by greed and by the love of money.
For the poor, that the Church may share her treasure with them.
For our group, that our hearts may rest in the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son's Heart has only one treasure, your will and our salvation. Make our hearts like his. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul boasts not of his visions but of his weakness: a thorn in the flesh that the Lord did not remove.
The Lord answered Paul's prayer: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”
Jesus tells us not to worry: look at the birds and the lilies, seek first God's kingdom, and let today's trouble be enough for today.
2027-06-19.action: Hand over one worry to God today in a short prayer each time it comes back to your mind.
2027-06-19.question: What do I serve first: God, or the security that money seems to promise?
kidsaint: St Romuald

Romuald was a rich young man in Italy about a thousand years ago. He was sad when he saw how much people fought and hurt each other, so he decided to give his life to God. He went to live as a monk, and later as a hermit, praying alone in a small hut in the hills. Many people came to learn from him, and he started many little houses of prayer, the most famous one at a place called Camaldoli. He taught his monks to sit quietly with God, as if they were already in paradise. Lesson: find a quiet minute every day to sit with God and tell him your worries.

family.explain: Jesus pointed to the birds and said: they do not plant rice or keep it in a store, but God feeds them. He pointed to the wild flowers and said: they do not sew clothes, but God dresses them more beautifully than a king. If God takes care of birds and flowers, he will surely take care of us. So we work hard, but we do not need to be afraid.
family.intention: We pray for families who are worried about school fees, rent or food this month, and for those who have lost work in the monsoon rains.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one worry in our family that we can give to God together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A young mother in Thrissur had saved for months for her children's school bags and uniforms, and then the monsoon flooded the ground floor of her house the week before school reopened. She sat on the stairs, she said later, counting what was lost. Her small son brought her a bird's feather he had found on the wet veranda and asked why birds do not get cold in the rain. She laughed for the first time that day, and remembered the Gospel of the birds of the air. Neighbours from the parish came the next morning with buckets and two old school bags. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you know our weakness and our worries. Let your grace be enough for us today, and teach us to seek first your kingdom. Amen.
share: A thorn was given me in the flesh (2 Corinthians 12:7). Is there a weakness in my life that God may be using to keep me humble and close to him?
My grace is sufficient for you (2 Corinthians 12:9). When have I experienced God's strength at a moment when I felt weakest?
Do not worry about tomorrow (Matthew 6:34). Which worry about tomorrow is stealing my peace today?
pm.resp: Taste and see the goodness of the Lord.
interc: For the sick and those who carry long illnesses, that they may find Christ's power in their weakness.
For parents anxious about the new school year, and for children beginning new classes, that they may trust the Father who feeds the birds.
For all who are tempted to serve money above God, that they may seek first his kingdom.
For monks, nuns and hermits, especially the Camaldolese, on the thousandth anniversary of St Romuald's death, that their prayer may sustain the Church.
For our group, that we may live one day at a time in the care of our heavenly Father.
pm.close: Father, you clothe the lilies and feed the birds of the air. Keep us in your care, and let the power of Christ dwell in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God calls Abram to leave his country, his kindred and his father's house, and promises that in him all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
Abram goes as the Lord told him, at seventy-five, and builds altars to the Lord wherever he stops.
Jesus warns against judging others: first take the log out of your own eye, then you will see clearly to help your brother.
2027-06-21.action: Take one small step today in something God has been asking of you, and hold back one harsh judgment.
2027-06-21.question: Do I see the speck in others' eyes more quickly than the log in my own?
kidsaint: St Aloysius Gonzaga

Aloysius was the son of a rich prince in Italy, and his father wanted him to become a great soldier. But Aloysius loved Jesus more than anything. When he was seventeen he gave his title and his money to his younger brother and joined the Jesuits to become a priest. When a terrible sickness spread through Rome, he went out to look after the sick people, washing them and carrying them to the hospital on his own back. He caught the sickness himself and died when he was only twenty-three. He is the patron saint of young people and students. Lesson: when you go back to school, ask St Aloysius to help you study well and to be kind to the weakest children in your class.

family.explain: God spoke to Abram and said: leave your home and go to a new land that I will show you. Abram did not know the way, but he trusted God and went. Wherever he stopped, he built an altar and prayed. God promised that through Abram all the families of the world would be blessed, and that promise came true in Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for children and teachers beginning the new school year, and for families who have had to move to a new place.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something hard God is asking our family to do? How can we trust him like Abram?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Kottayam had a good job offer in the Gulf and a call, which he could not shake off, to serve as a lay missionary for two years in a tribal school in Odisha. His father was angry: we spent everything on your studies, and now you want to teach in a village? He went to the parish priest, who read him Genesis 12 and said: Abram did not have a map either. He went. Years later, back in Kerala with a family of his own, he said those two years taught him more about God than all his engineering. His father, who had come to visit him in Odisha, became the school's most faithful donor. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you called Abraham and he went. Give us faith to follow your call, humility to see our own faults, and the joy of St Aloysius in serving others. Amen.
share: Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house (Genesis 12:1). What is God asking me to leave behind in order to follow him more closely?
So Abram went, as the Lord had told him (Genesis 12:4). When have I obeyed God without knowing where it would lead, and what did I find?
First take the log out of your own eye (Matthew 7:5). Whom have I been judging harshly, and what log do I need to remove first?
pm.resp: Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
interc: For the Church, the family of Abraham's faith, that she may be a blessing to all the families of the earth.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For students and teachers at the start of the school year, through the prayers of St Aloysius, patron of youth.
For migrants and families who have left their homeland in search of work or safety, that they may find welcome.
For our group, that we may stop judging others and begin by examining our own hearts.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to your promises from age to age. Lead us on our pilgrimage, as you led Abraham, and make us a blessing for others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: When strife arises between their herders, Abram chooses peace with Lot, saying: we are kindred, and gives the younger man the first choice of land.
Lot chooses the well-watered plain toward Sodom; God then promises Abram all the land he can see and offspring like the dust of the earth.
Jesus teaches: do not give what is holy to dogs; do to others as you would have them do to you; enter through the narrow gate.
