Lot chooses the green, well-watered plain, near Sodom. It looks good, but it leads him into trouble. Abram takes what is left. And then God says to him: raise your eyes and look in every direction; all the land that you see I will give to you (Genesis 13:14–15). The one who let go for the sake of peace receives everything from God.

In the Gospel Jesus gives the rule that Abram lived: in everything do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). It is simple to say and hard to do. And he warns that the road to life is narrow: the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and there are few who find it (Matthew 7:14).

St John Fisher and St Thomas More, whom we may remember today, chose that narrow gate. When the king demanded an oath against their conscience and against unity with the Pope, almost everyone took it. They refused, and gave their lives. Today, let us ask for their courage, and for Abram's generosity. If there is a quarrel in our family over land or money, let us be the first to say: let there be no strife between us, for we are kindred. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever fought with your brother or sister over a toy, or the best seat, or the biggest piece of cake? Abram and his nephew Lot had a fight between their shepherds. Abram said: let us not fight, we are family. You choose first! Jesus gave us a golden rule: do to others what you would like them to do to you. Today, try to let someone else choose first, and see how happy it makes them, and Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, Abram had left everything at God's word, and years later he still had no child. So he says to God: what will you give me, for I continue childless? (Genesis 15:2). It is a very honest prayer. Many of us have prayed like that: Lord, I have done everything you asked, and still I am waiting.

God does not scold him. He takes him outside and says: look toward heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them. So shall your descendants be (Genesis 15:5). Nothing had changed in Abram's tent. But he lifted his eyes from his problem to God's sky. And he believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6). This is faith: not seeing, but trusting the One who promises.

Then God makes a covenant. In those days, people who made a treaty walked between animals cut in two, as if to say: may this happen to me if I break my word. But that night only God passes between the pieces, as a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch. God binds himself alone. His faithfulness does not depend on ours. The Psalm sings: he is mindful of his covenant forever (Psalm 105:8).

In the Gospel Jesus says: beware of false prophets; you will know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:15–16). Not every attractive preacher is a true prophet. Look at the fruit: love, humility, peace, unity. Tomorrow we celebrate the birth of John the Baptist, a true prophet, whose fruit was to point to Jesus. This evening many parishes begin the feast with the Vigil Mass. Let us also prepare: lift up our eyes like Abram, believe God's promise, and let our faith bear good fruit. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever tried to count the stars at night? You cannot, there are too many! God told Abram: your family will be as many as the stars. Abram was old and had no children, but he believed God. And God kept his promise. Jesus said: a good tree gives good fruit. When we believe in God, we should give good fruit too: being kind, sharing, saying sorry. Tonight, look up at the sky and say: God, I believe you!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is a birthday. The Church usually remembers saints on the day they died, their birthday into heaven. But today, as on Christmas and on Our Lady's birthday, we celebrate a birth: the birth of John the Baptist. Even before he was born, John was filled with the Holy Spirit. When Mary came to visit Elizabeth, carrying Jesus within her, the baby John leapt for joy. He was rejoicing in Jesus before he saw the light of day.

The first reading speaks of God's servant: the Lord called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me (Isaiah 49:1). And the Psalm says: you knit me together in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made (Psalm 139:13–14). This is true of John, and it is true of every one of us. Before your parents saw your face, God knew you. Every child in the womb is a person loved by God. Today we pray for all mothers expecting a child, and for all babies not yet born.

In the Gospel the whole village rejoices with Elizabeth, who had waited so long for a child. On the eighth day the relatives want to call him Zechariah, after his father. But Elizabeth says: no; he is to be called John. And Zechariah, who could not speak, writes on a tablet: his name is John (Luke 1:63). The name means: the Lord has shown favour. This child belongs not to the family's plans but to God's grace. And at once Zechariah's mouth is opened, and he praises God.

Zechariah had been silent because he doubted the angel's message. Now his silence turns into a song, the Benedictus, which the Church sings every morning. Perhaps some of us have become silent before God because of disappointment or doubt. Today God wants to open our mouths again to praise him.

Everyone asked: what then will this child become? (Luke 1:66). He became the greatest of the prophets. And what was his greatness? St Paul tells us in the second reading. John said: I am not he. One is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of the sandals on his feet (Acts 13:25). John's greatness was his humility. He pointed away from himself to Jesus: he must increase, but I must decrease.

At every Mass we hear John's words again, when the priest lifts the Host and says: Behold the Lamb of God. Let us ask John the Baptist today to teach us his joy and his humility. Let us praise God for the gift of life, protect every child, and point others not to ourselves but to Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, today is John the Baptist's birthday! His parents were very old, and they thought they would never have a baby. But God gave them a son. Everyone said: call him Zechariah, like his papa. But his mother said: no, his name is John! And his papa, who could not talk, wrote: His name is John. Then he could talk again, and he sang a happy song to God.

Even before John was born, he jumped for joy when Mary came near with baby Jesus. When he grew up, he pointed to Jesus and said: Look, there is the Lamb of God! You can be like John: whenever you can, help your friends to know Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, Abraham is ninety-nine years old. For twenty-four years he has waited for the son God promised. Then God speaks again: I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be blameless (Genesis 17:1). God gives him a new name, Abraham, father of a multitude. And he gives Sarai a new name too, Sarah. A new name means a new beginning, even at ninety-nine.

And what does Abraham do when God promises a son by Sarah? He falls on his face and laughs. Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? (Genesis 17:17). We understand him. We too sometimes laugh quietly at God's promises, or we offer God an easier plan, like Abraham offering Ishmael. But God says: your wife Sarah shall bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac. Isaac means he laughs. God turns the laugh of doubt into the laugh of joy.

In the Gospel Jesus comes down from the mountain, and a leper comes to him. By the Law he had to live alone, outside the village, crying unclean. Nobody touched him. He kneels and says: Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean (Matthew 8:2). What a beautiful prayer. He does not command Jesus. He trusts both his power and his will.

And Jesus stretches out his hand and touches him. I do choose. Be made clean! (Matthew 8:3). The hand that touched the leper is the hand of the Sacred Heart, whom we honour this month. He chooses to heal, to cleanse, to bring us back. Today let us bring him the thing we have stopped hoping for, and let us stretch out our own hands to someone nobody touches. Amen.
kids: Children, a long time ago Abraham and Sarah were very, very old, and God said: you will have a baby boy! Abraham laughed. A baby at a hundred years? But God kept his promise, and the baby was called Isaac, which means he laughs. In the Gospel a sick man came to Jesus. Nobody wanted to go near him. But Jesus touched him and made him well. Jesus loves to touch and heal the ones nobody wants. Let us be kind to the child who is left alone at school!

homily: Dear friends, picture the scene. It is the hottest part of the day. Old Abraham is sitting at the door of his tent. He looks up and sees three strangers. And this man of ninety-nine years runs to meet them, bows down, brings water for their feet, has bread baked and a calf prepared, and stands beside them like a servant while they eat (Genesis 18:1–8). He does not know who they are. But the Bible tells us: the Lord appeared to Abraham. When he welcomed strangers, he welcomed God.

Then the visitor says: your wife Sarah shall have a son. Sarah is listening behind the tent, and she laughs to herself. I am old, my husband is old. And the Lord asks: why did Sarah laugh? Is anything too wonderful for the Lord? (Genesis 18:14). That is the question of today. Is anything too wonderful for him? Is your family situation too difficult? Is your sin too great? Is your sorrow too deep? Nothing is too wonderful for the Lord.

Centuries later an angel said the same thing to a young girl in Nazareth: nothing will be impossible with God. Sarah laughed and hid. Mary believed, and sang the song we prayed today as our psalm: the Mighty One has done great things for me. On this Saturday let us ask Mary to teach us her faith.

And in the Gospel a Roman officer shows us that faith can be found where we least expect it. Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only speak the word (Matthew 8:8). We say his words at every Mass. Let us say them today with his faith, carrying to Jesus the people we love. His word is enough. Amen.
kids: Children, one very hot day Abraham saw three visitors coming. He ran to meet them, gave them water and bread and a big meal. Guess who was visiting? God himself! Then God said: Sarah, you will have a baby. Sarah laughed, because she was very old. But God said: is anything too hard for the Lord? No! Nothing is too hard for God. And when visitors come to your house, be kind and share, like Abraham!

homily: Dear friends, God says something beautiful in today's first reading: shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do? (Genesis 18:17). God treats Abraham as a friend, and tells him that he is going down to see the sin of Sodom. And Abraham does what friends of God do. He does not say: good, they deserve it. He stays standing before the Lord, and he prays for the city.

Listen to his prayer. Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Suppose there are fifty righteous. And when God agrees, he goes on: forty-five? forty? thirty? twenty? ten? He calls himself dust and ashes, but he does not stop. And each time God says yes. God is more ready to forgive than Abraham is to ask. The prayer of a righteous person, even for a wicked city, is precious to God.

This is a lesson for us. We complain a lot about our towns, our politics, our young people. Do we pray for them as much as we complain? Abraham stopped at ten. But God found one righteous man, Jesus, and for his sake he forgives all who turn to him. When we pray for others, we stand beside Jesus, the great intercessor.

In the Gospel Jesus tells those who want to follow him: the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head (Matthew 8:20). St Irenaeus, whom we honour today, took that seriously. He left his home in Asia, went to the far west, served the Church in Lyons in a time of persecution, and spent his life guarding the faith handed down from the apostles. He said: the glory of God is a human being fully alive. Today let us be fully alive in prayer for others, and in following Jesus without delay. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham was God's friend. One day God told him that a city called Sodom was very, very bad. Abraham did not say: good, punish them! He prayed for them. He asked God: if there are fifty good people, will you save the city? Then forty? Thirty? Ten? And God said yes every time! When you hear about people doing wrong, do not just say they are bad. Pray for them, like Abraham!

homily: Dear friends, today's first reading is a hard story. At last Isaac is born, the son of the promise. But in the same house there is another boy, Ishmael, the son of the slave woman Hagar. Sarah wants them sent away. Abraham is deeply distressed, because Ishmael is his son too. And early in the morning Hagar and her boy are sent into the desert with a little bread and a skin of water.

The water runs out. Hagar lays the child under a bush, goes a bowshot away and weeps, because she cannot watch him die. And then the Bible says: God heard the voice of the boy (Genesis 21:17). Do not be afraid. God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. The well was there all the time. She could not see it through her tears. How often that happens to us. We are so full of fear that we do not see the help God has already placed beside us.

And notice whom God hears: not the important people at the feast, but a foreign slave woman and a crying child in the desert. Ishmael's name means God hears. Our God is the God who hears the poor. If we want to be his people, we must hear them too: the migrant worker, the abandoned mother, the child who cries at night.

In the Gospel Jesus delivers two men who lived among the tombs. A whole herd of pigs is lost. And the people of the town come out and beg Jesus to leave. They preferred their pigs to their neighbours' deliverance, and their business to the Son of God. Today we also remember the first martyrs of Rome, who were burned and crucified under Nero. They did the opposite of the Gadarenes: they lost everything rather than lose Jesus. Let us ask for their courage, and let us never ask the Lord to leave. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother named Hagar and her little boy Ishmael were walking in the hot desert. Their water was finished, and the boy was crying. His mother was crying too. But God heard the boy! An angel said: do not be afraid. God opened Hagar's eyes and she saw a well full of water! God always hears children when they cry. So when you are sad or afraid, talk to God. He is listening.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.”
God's question in the garden, the first promise of victory, the stronger one who binds the strong man, and the new family of Jesus.

sub: Afraid of the God who loves us.
q: But the Lord God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
points.apply: Make an examination of conscience this week without excuses, and go to confession.

q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
The Son of God was revealed for this purpose, to destroy the works of the devil.
points.apply: When temptation comes this week, call on the name of Jesus and ask the prayers of Mary, who crushed the serpent's head with her Son.

q: If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, Lord, who could stand? But there is forgiveness with you, so that you may be revered.
But no one can enter a strong man's house and plunder his property without first tying up the strong man; then indeed the house can be plundered.
points.apply: Name one habit of sin that holds you captive and bring it to Christ in confession; he is stronger.

sub: His mother and his brothers outside.
Doing the will of God, like Mary.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Each morning this week ask, Lord, what is your will for me today? and each evening, Did I do it?

concl: God seeks us when we hide and promises from the beginning a victory over the serpent through the offspring of the woman.
Jesus, the stronger one, binds the strong man and gathers a new family of those who do the will of God; Mary is the first of them, and we do not lose heart.
2027-06-06.resolve: Come out of hiding this week: make a good confession and begin each day by asking to do God's will.

intro: Theme: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
The sea that God sets within bounds, the Lord asleep in the boat, the word that calms the storm, and the love that makes us a new creation.

sub: God answers Job from the whirlwind.
q: Thus far shall you come, and no farther, and here shall your proud waves be stopped
We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose.
points.apply: Write down the storm you are facing and, beneath it, Job 38:11; pray it each evening this week.

sub: The waves beat into the boat.
q: He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
But he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and said to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
points.apply: When you feel that God is silent, keep praying honestly, as the disciples did; do not stop calling him.

sub: A holy fear: who then is this?
q: he made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
And they were filled with great awe and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
points.apply: Make an act of faith in the divinity of Christ this week, at the elevation of the Host: My Lord and my God.

points.h: The love of Christ urges us on
q: I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it?
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Do one act of love this week for someone outside your circle, remembering that Christ died for that person too.

concl: The God who set bounds to the sea is the Lord asleep in our boat; he commands the storm and asks for our faith.
Christ, who died and rose for all, makes us a new creation, and his love urges us to live for him.
2027-06-20.resolve: Pray each day this week for someone in a storm, and for fishermen at sea and for fathers.

intro: Theme: “Do not fear, only believe.”
God did not make death; Christ touches the sick with life and takes the dead by the hand; and his grace makes us generous.

sub: God on the side of life.
q: because God did not make death, and he does not delight in the death of the living.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
points.apply: Pray this week for someone who is dying, and for the grace of a holy death for yourself.

q: O Lord my God, I cried to you for help, and you have healed me.
He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace, and be healed of your disease.”
points.apply: At each Communion this week, make a conscious act of faith before you receive.

q: You have turned my mourning into dancing; you have taken off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy,
He took her by the hand and said to her, “Talitha cum,” which means, “Little girl, get up!”
points.apply: When bad news comes this week, before anything else say: Jesus, I believe; do not let me fear.

q: those who gathered much had nothing over, and those who gathered little had no shortage; they gathered as much as each of them needed.
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Give generously to Peter's Pence or to a family in need this week, as a thank-offering for the grace of Christ.

concl: God created us for life; death came through the devil's envy, and Jesus shows that he is stronger than sickness and death.
The woman's touch and Jairus' trust teach us to come to him with faith, and his poverty teaches us to share.
2027-06-27.resolve: Visit or call one sick person this week, pray with them, and give something to the poor in thanksgiving.

intro: Theme: “But who do you say that I am?”
The faith of Peter, the keys of the kingdom, the praying Church, and Paul's race finished: two pillars of one Church.

points.h: Who do you say that I am?
sub: A confession revealed by the Father.
q: See, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation: “One who trusts will not panic.”
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
points.apply: Write your own answer to Jesus' question and pray it each morning this week.

sub: The key of the house of David.
q: I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David; he shall open, and no one shall shut; he shall shut, and no one shall open.
And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
points.apply: Pray every day this week for Pope Leo XIV, and read one short text of his teaching.

sub: The gate that opened of its own accord.
q: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
While Peter was kept in prison, the church prayed fervently to God for him.
points.apply: Choose one persecuted Christian community and pray for it fervently each day this week.

sub: The fight, the race, the faith.
q: I sought the Lord, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness,
points.apply: Name the race you are tempted to abandon, and take one step this week to keep running it.

concl: Peter confesses Christ and receives the keys; on his faith and his ministry, continued in his successors, Christ builds his Church.
Paul runs the race to the end and keeps the faith; with both apostles we confess the Son of the living God.
2027-06-29.resolve: Pray each day this week for the Pope and for persecuted Christians, and renew your own confession of faith.

intro: Theme: “The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.”
The cedar God himself replants, the seed that grows by itself, the smallest of all seeds, and the life of faith that waits for the harvest.

q: I myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of a cedar; I will set it out. I will break off a tender one from the topmost of its young twigs; I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.
points.apply: Bring to God in prayer one part of your life that seems broken, and ask him to plant something new there.

q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty,
The kingdom of God is as if someone would scatter seed on the ground, and would sleep and rise night and day, and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.
points.apply: Keep praying for someone in whom you see no change, and thank God each day for the growth you cannot see.

points.h: The smallest of all the seeds
sub: A garden plant, not a mighty cedar.
q: For whoever has despised the day of small things shall rejoice,

It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth; yet when it is sown it grows up and becomes the greatest of all shrubs, and puts forth large branches, so that the birds of the air can make nests in its shade.
points.apply: Do one small thing for the kingdom this week that no one will notice: a visit, a gift, a hidden prayer.

sub: At home in the body, away from the Lord.
The harvest before the judgment seat.
q: The righteous flourish like the palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon. They are planted in the house of the Lord; they flourish in the courts of our God. In old age they still produce fruit; they are always green and full of sap,
for we walk by faith, not by sight.
points.apply: Each night this week, before sleeping, ask: what did I sow today that will please the Lord at the harvest?

concl: God plants, the seed grows by his power, and the kingdom begins small but shelters all.
Our part is to sow in faith, to wait in patience and to live so as to please the Lord until the harvest.
2027-06-13.resolve: Sow one seed of faith or kindness each day this week, and leave the growth to God.

intro: Theme: “Give … to God the things that are God's.”
A good man humbled in the dark, a coin that bears Caesar's face, and a philosopher who gave God his life.

points.h: A good man in the dark
q: Then she replied to me, “Where are your acts of charity? Where are your righteous deeds? These things are known about you!”
Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.
points.apply: Notice where suffering or tiredness has made you suspicious or harsh at home, and say one word of trust or thanks to the person you have hurt.

q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
Give to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's.
points.apply: Be an honest citizen this week, in taxes, bills and work; and give God the first place in your day, because you bear his image.

sub: Loyal to the emperor in what is lawful.
q: Happy are those who fear the Lord, who greatly delight in his commandments.
For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
points.apply: Learn one reason for your faith this week, so that you can give an answer with gentleness when someone asks.

concl: Tobit shows us a good man made hard by suffering, whom God will heal; Jesus shows us that the coin belongs to Caesar but the person belongs to God.
St Justin lived both: an honest citizen and a faithful witness, who gave God what bears God's image, his whole life.
2027-06-01.resolve: Each morning this week, before anything else, say: Lord, I am yours; and then be kind at home.

intro: Theme: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.”
Two prayers from the depths, heard at the same moment, and the faithfulness of God that is stronger than death.

q: You are righteous, O Lord, and all your deeds are just; all your ways are mercy and truth; you judge the world.
Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness; for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but that very Spirit intercedes with sighs too deep for words.
points.apply: When you feel at the bottom this week, pray anyway: begin with one line of praise, then tell God the truth.

sub: Life given where death was asked.
q: At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard in the glorious presence of God.
Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Write down one prayer you are praying now, and keep it; look back in a year to see how God answered.

sub: I am the God of Abraham.
q: He said further, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”
He is God not of the dead, but of the living; you are quite wrong.
points.apply: Pray for your beloved dead by name this week, and have a Mass offered for one of them if you can.

concl: Tobit and Sarah prayed from the depths and asked to die; God heard them at that very moment and sent healing and life.
Jesus teaches that God is faithful beyond death: he is the God of the living, and his promises reach beyond the grave.
2027-06-02.resolve: Each evening this week, lift up your soul to God with the words of Psalm 25, and pray for one person who has died.

intro: Theme: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart.”
A wedding night that begins in prayer, the first and second commandments, and young martyrs who loved God more than life.

points.h: A marriage that begins on its knees
sub: Sister, get up, and let us pray.
q: I now am taking this kinswoman of mine, not because of lust, but with sincerity. Grant that she and I may find mercy and that we may grow old together.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her,
points.apply: Married couples: pray together tonight, even one Our Father. Others: pray for one couple you know who is struggling.

sub: With heart, soul, mind and strength.
q: Hear, O Israel: The Lord is our God, the Lord alone. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
You are not far from the kingdom of God.
points.apply: Pray the Shema slowly each morning this week, then do one deliberate act of love for a neighbour.

q: Happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
points.apply: Pray this week for young people in your parish who are pressured to do wrong, and encourage one of them by name.

concl: Tobias and Sarah show us love that puts God first and so loves the other purely; Jesus names that order as the heart of the Law.
The martyrs of Uganda loved God with all their strength and kept their purity to the point of death; their blood has become the seed of a great Church.
2027-06-03.resolve: Put God first each day this week: begin the morning with the Shema and end the evening with a prayer together with your family.

intro: Theme: “They will look on the one whom they have pierced.”
The heart of a Father that recoils from anger, the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, and the pierced side from which the Church is born.

points.h: The heart that recoils from anger
sub: A parent teaching a child to walk.
q: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, O Israel? … My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender.
In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
points.apply: If you think of God as always angry with you, read Hosea 11 slowly this week and let him lift you to his cheek.

q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
Let anyone who is thirsty come to me,
points.apply: Draw from the wells this month: plan a confession and a First Friday Communion, and come to them thirsty.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
points.apply: Pray Paul's prayer (Ephesians 3:14–19) for your family each night this week, using their names.

sub: The Lamb whose bones are not broken.
The Church born from his side.
q: when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child,
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Make an act of reparation this week: an hour of adoration, a visit to someone lonely, or a gentle answer where you used to be harsh.

concl: God's heart, Hosea tells us, recoils from anger and burns with compassion; in Jesus that heart became a human heart, and on the Cross it was opened for us.
From the pierced side flow the sacraments and the Church; we answer with love, reparation, prayer for priests, and hearts made gentle and humble like his.
2027-06-04.resolve: Renew your family's consecration to the Sacred Heart this month and keep the First Fridays faithfully.

intro: Theme: “His mother treasured all these things in her heart.”
The Immaculate Heart of Mary: clothed in salvation, searching in love, keeping the Word, and giving everything.

sub: Clothed with the garments of salvation.
q: My heart exults in the Lord; my strength is exalted in my God.
My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,
points.apply: Begin each day this week by praying the Magnificat, slowly, and thank God for one way he has lifted you up.

q: I will rise now and go about the city, in the streets and in the squares; I will seek him whom my soul loves.
Child, why have you treated us like this? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.
points.apply: If you have drifted from Jesus, search for him this week where Mary found him: in his Father's house, at Mass and in confession.

q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
points.apply: Learn one verse of today's Gospel by heart and repeat it whenever you do not understand what God is doing.

q: It is better to give alms than to lay up gold.
For all of them have contributed out of their abundance; but she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on.
points.apply: Consecrate yourself and your family to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, and give one generous gift to someone in need.

concl: Mary's Heart is Immaculate not because it feels nothing, but because it feels everything with faith and love, without sin.
She teaches us to exult in God, to search for Jesus, to keep his word when we do not understand, and to give him everything.
2027-06-05.resolve: Make the five First Saturdays, beginning today if you can, and pray the Magnificat each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “The God of all consolation.”
A God who comforts us in affliction, a comfort that flows on to others, and the upside-down happiness of the Beatitudes.

sub: Paul begins with blessing, not complaint.
God meets us inside our affliction.
q: Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God.
For just as the sufferings of Christ are abundant for us, so also our consolation is abundant through Christ.
points.apply: Tonight, recall one hard moment in your life when God comforted you, and thank him for it by name.

sub: Comfort is not a private treasure.
The Church as a community of consolation.
q: The Lord is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.
Our hope for you is unshaken; for we know that as you share in our sufferings, so also you share in our consolation.
points.apply: This week visit or call one person who is going through a trial you have known yourself.

sub: Blessed are the poor in spirit.
q: O taste and see that the Lord is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
points.apply: Choose one Beatitude for this week and ask the Lord each morning to help you live it.

concl: Paul blesses the God of all consolation, who comforts us in every trouble so that we can comfort others.
Jesus calls blessed the poor, the mourners and the meek, because God's kingdom and God's comfort belong to them.
2027-06-07.resolve: Each day this week, pass on to one person the comfort God has given you.

intro: Theme: “In him it is always Yes.”
God's faithful Yes in Christ, the seal of the Spirit on the baptised, and the salt and light that must not be hidden.

sub: Our plans change; God's word does not.
q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he promised, and will he not do it?
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.” For this reason it is through him that we say the “Amen,” to the glory of God.
points.apply: Today keep one promise you have made to God or to someone in your family, without excuses.

sub: The chrism of Baptism and Confirmation.
The Spirit as a first installment.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
But it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, by putting his seal on us and giving us his Spirit in our hearts as a first installment.
points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and Confirmation and thank God for them on those days each year.

sub: A gift before it is a task.
A lamp on the stand, glory to the Father.
q: The unfolding of your words gives light; it imparts understanding to the simple.
You are the salt of the earth; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored?
points.apply: This week, do one good work openly in your parish or neighbourhood, and give the credit to God.

concl: In Jesus Christ every promise of God is Yes, and through him we answer Amen; by the Spirit we are anointed and sealed as God's own.
Jesus calls his disciples salt and light, and asks that our good works shine so that the Father may be glorified.
2027-06-08.resolve: Let your yes be faithful and your light visible: one kept promise and one good work each day this week.

intro: Theme: “The Spirit gives life.”
A letter written on hearts, the holy Law fulfilled and not abolished, and the Spirit who makes us keep it with love.

sub: Not with ink but with the Spirit.
q: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you are to speak.
Not that we are competent of ourselves to claim anything as coming from us; our competence is from God,
points.apply: Before any task of service this week, pray: Lord, my competence is from you.

sub: Stone tablets and hearts of flesh.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.
points.apply: Choose one commandment you find hard and pray each day this week for the Spirit to write it on your heart.

points.h: Not to abolish but to fulfill
sub: Not one stroke of a letter.
The Harp of the Spirit sings it.
q: The law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the soul; the decrees of the Lord are sure, making wise the simple;

Therefore, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments, and teaches others to do the same, will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Teach one child, by word or example, one of God's commandments this week.

concl: Paul's ministry is the work of the Spirit, who writes God's holy Law on human hearts and gives life.
Jesus fulfils the Law and the prophets; St Ephrem teaches us to sing that fulfilment with our whole life.
2027-06-09.resolve: Each day this week, keep one commandment from the heart, and thank the Spirit who makes it possible.

intro: Theme: “From one degree of glory to another.”
A veil removed, a face transformed by the glory of Christ, and a peace made before the altar.

q: Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
but when one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.
points.apply: Each day this week read a short passage of the Gospel, asking first: Lord, remove the veil.

sub: Light in the face of Christ.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.
points.apply: Spend five minutes today before the Blessed Sacrament or a crucifix, simply looking at the Lord and letting him look at you.

sub: Anger is the root of murder.
q: Steadfast love and faithfulness will meet; righteousness and peace will kiss each other.
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
points.apply: Before Sunday, take one step towards peace with someone, and make the sign of peace at Mass with that person in your heart.

concl: When we turn to the Lord the veil falls, and we are changed from glory to glory into the image of Christ, in whose face God's light shines.
Jesus asks for a righteousness that reaches the heart: no anger nursed, no insult spoken, and reconciliation before we offer our gift.
2027-06-10.resolve: This week, end one quarrel and let the light of Christ shine through the peace you make.

intro: Theme: “A good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.”
The son of encouragement: eyes that rejoice in grace, humility that makes room for others, and a life given without payment.

sub: He saw the grace of God and rejoiced.
He exhorted them to remain faithful.
q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Say to those who are of a fearful heart, “Be strong, do not fear!”
There was a Levite, a native of Cyprus, Joseph, to whom the apostles gave the name Barnabas (which means “son of encouragement”).
points.apply: Each day this week, give one sincere word of encouragement to someone who is struggling.

points.h: He went to look for Saul
q: Saul's son Jonathan set out and came to David at Horesh; there he strengthened his hand through the Lord.
But Barnabas took him, brought him to the apostles, and described for them how on the road he had seen the Lord, who had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
points.apply: Think of one person whose gifts you could bring forward in your parish or workplace, and do it this week.

q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Pray this week for one missionary you know by name, and offer some help to the missions.

concl: Barnabas saw the grace of God in others and rejoiced, made room for Saul's gifts and gave Mark a second chance.
Set apart by the Spirit in a praying, fasting Church, he gave without payment what he had received, to the end.
2027-06-11.resolve: This week, be a Barnabas: encourage one person each day and give one service without seeking any return.

intro: Theme: “Everything has become new.”
The love of Christ that urges us on, the new creation and the ministry of reconciliation, and the simple Yes of the disciple.

points.h: The love of Christ urges us on
sub: Seeing no one from a human point of view.
q: I led them with cords of human kindness, with bands of love.
And he died for all, so that those who live might live no longer for themselves, but for him who died and was raised for them.
points.apply: This week, do one thing each day that you would not do for yourself, simply for the love of Christ.

q: as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.
So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making his appeal through us; we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
points.apply: Make a good confession this week, and invite one person to come with you.

sub: A word that can be trusted.
q: Those who walk blamelessly, and do what is right, and speak the truth from their heart;
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
points.apply: For this week, give up the habit of swearing or exaggerating, and keep every small promise you make.

concl: Christ died for all so that we might live for him; in him we are a new creation, reconciled to God and sent as his ambassadors.
Jesus asks for a simple and truthful word; Mary's Yes shows us how to answer God.
2027-06-12.resolve: This week, be reconciled to God in confession, and let your yes be yes and your no be no.

intro: Theme: “If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.”
The day of salvation is today, the paradoxes of the apostle, and the goodness that breaks the chain of revenge.

sub: Do not receive grace in vain.
q: Thus says the Lord: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you;
See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Do this week the good thing you have been postponing: a confession, a reconciliation, a visit to the sick.

q: Though the fig tree does not blossom, and no fruit is on the vines; though the produce of the olive fails, and the fields yield no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls, yet I will rejoice in the Lord; I will exult in the God of my salvation.
as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
points.apply: Thank God this week for one loss or hardship through which he has made you richer in faith.

sub: An eye for an eye: a limit on revenge.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink;
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Answer one insult or unfair demand this week with an unexpected act of kindness.

concl: Grace is offered today: the apostle who has Christ possesses everything, even in poverty and pain.
Jesus breaks the chain of revenge with a stronger force, the goodness that goes the second mile.
2027-06-14.resolve: Each day this week, do one thing more than you were asked, with love.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
The generosity of the poor, the poverty of Christ that makes us rich, and the Father's love that falls like rain on all.

sub: Joy and poverty overflowing in generosity.
The generous act of our Lord.
q: who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry.
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Give something this week from your own need, not only from what you have left over, and give it with joy.

sub: The Father's love does not choose.
q: When you come upon your enemy's ox or donkey going astray, you shall bring it back.
But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven;
points.apply: Do one practical kindness this week for someone who does not like you.

sub: Merciful as the Father is merciful.
Every Christian is called to holiness.
q: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
points.apply: Each evening this week ask: where was I merciful today, and where did I fail to be?

concl: The poor of Macedonia gave beyond their means because they had first given themselves; Christ became poor to make us rich.
The Father's love falls like rain on all; we become his children when we love our enemies and pray for those who hurt us.
2027-06-15.resolve: Pray every day this week, by name, for one person who has hurt you.

intro: Theme: “Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
Giving as sowing, the cheerful heart God loves, and the hidden life of alms, prayer and fasting.

sub: The God who supplies seed to the sower.
q: If you have many possessions, make your gift from them in proportion; if few, do not be afraid to give according to the little you have.
The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
points.apply: Set aside a fixed part of your income this month for the poor, and give it before you spend on yourself.

q: They have given to the poor; their righteousness endures forever;
Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
points.apply: Give one gift this week with a smile and without telling anyone.

sub: Alms, prayer and fasting for the Father.
q: O Lord, you have searched me and known me.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Choose one hidden practice this week: a secret alms, a quiet prayer behind a shut door, or a small fast offered for someone in need.

concl: Giving is sowing, and God loves the glad heart that gives without reluctance.
Alms, prayer and fasting are done for the Father who sees in secret, not for the applause of others.
2027-06-16.resolve: Do one good deed each day this week that only God will know about.

intro: Theme: “Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.”
A Church betrothed to Christ alone, prayer without empty words, and the prayer that sums up the Gospel.

sub: Paul as friend of the Bridegroom.
q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises privately this week, and name one false god you want to renounce.

q: Never be rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be quick to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven, and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few.

When you are praying, do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard because of their many words. Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silent prayer each day this week, saying only: Father, you know.

sub: His name, his kingdom, his will.
q: For you are our father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us; you, O Lord, are our father; our Redeemer from of old is your name.
Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father as a family every evening this week, slowly, and forgive one another before you begin.

concl: Paul longs to keep the Church a chaste bride for Christ; prayer keeps our hearts undivided.
Jesus teaches us to pray with few words and a child's trust, putting the Father first and forgiving as we are forgiven.
2027-06-17.resolve: Pray the Our Father slowly every day this week, and mean every word.

intro: Theme: “Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
The apostle who boasts of weakness, the treasure that lasts, and the eye that fills life with light.

sub: Labours, dangers and daily anxiety for the churches.
q: Thus says the Lord: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth; but let those who boast boast in this, that they understand and know me,
but he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So, I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
points.apply: Offer to Christ one weakness you are ashamed of, and ask him to show his power there.

sub: Riches that no one can steal.
q: if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Look at how you spent your money last month, and move one part of it this month to the poor or the Church.

sub: A heart drawn to the Sacred Heart.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
The eye is the lamp of the body. So, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light;
points.apply: Each day this week, spend five minutes before the Blessed Sacrament or an image of the Sacred Heart, giving him your heart.

concl: Paul's glory is his weakness, through which the power of Christ shines.
Our heart follows our treasure: let it be in heaven, in the Heart of Jesus, and our whole life will be full of light.
2027-06-18.resolve: This week, give away one thing you are attached to, and give your heart to Jesus each day.

intro: Theme: “My grace is sufficient for you.”
A thorn that stayed, a grace that came, and a Father who feeds the birds and clothes the lilies.

sub: Visions Paul will not boast of.
q: He gives power to the faint, and strengthens the powerless.
Three times I appealed to the Lord about this, that it would leave me,
points.apply: Pray today for the grace to carry the burden God has not yet taken away, instead of only asking him to remove it.

sub: Weakness as a dwelling for Christ.
When I am weak, then I am strong.
q: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
Therefore I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities for the sake of Christ; for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
points.apply: Thank God this week for one weakness through which you have come to depend on him more.

q: O taste and see that the Lord is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
points.apply: Begin each morning this week with a short prayer giving the day to God before you look at your phone or your accounts.

concl: Paul learned that grace is sufficient and that Christ's power lives in our weakness.
Jesus teaches us to seek first the kingdom and to leave tomorrow in the Father's hands.
2027-06-19.resolve: Give one worry to God each day this week, and do today's work in peace.

intro: Theme: “So Abram went, as the Lord had told him.”
A call to leave and a promise to bless, and a Lord who asks us to look at our own eye first, as St Aloysius did.

points.h: Go, to the land I will show you
q: Now the Lord said to Abram, “Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.”
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Take one concrete step this week in obedience to something God has long been asking of you.

points.h: A blessing for all the families of the earth
q: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who curses you I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, declared the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying, “All the Gentiles shall be blessed in you.”
points.apply: Be a blessing to one family outside your own this week, by a visit, a meal or a word of encouragement.

sub: Honest with ourselves, merciful to others.
q: for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your neighbor's eye.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience before your next confession, looking at your own faults rather than at those of others.

concl: Abraham went at God's word, and through him God began to bless all the families of the earth.
Jesus asks us to judge ourselves honestly and others mercifully; St Aloysius shows us how, strict with himself and gentle with all.
2027-06-21.resolve: Take one step of obedience to God this week and refuse one harsh judgment each day.

intro: Theme: “Let there be no strife between you and me, for we are kindred.”
Abram chooses peace over property, God blesses the one who lets go, and Jesus gives the golden rule and the narrow gate.

points.h: No strife, for we are kindred
sub: The elder gives the first choice.
q: Then Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herders and my herders; for we are kindred.
If it is possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all.
points.apply: Be the first to speak a word of peace in a quarrel in your family or neighbourhood this week.

sub: Lot looks with the eyes of the market.
The one who lets go receives.
q: Raise your eyes now, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward; for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.
Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
points.apply: Before a big decision this week, ask not only what looks best but what is best for your soul and your family.

points.h: The golden rule and the narrow gate
sub: Few find the narrow road: Fisher and More.
q: O Lord, who may abide in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy hill? Those who walk blamelessly, and do what is right, and speak the truth from their heart;
In everything do to others as you would have them do to you; for this is the law and the prophets.
points.apply: Choose one situation at home or at work this week where you will act by the golden rule even if it costs you.

concl: Abram chose peace with his kinsman over the best land, and God gave him more than he gave up.
Jesus asks us to do to others what we want for ourselves and to walk the narrow road, as Sts John Fisher and Thomas More did.
2027-06-22.resolve: Make peace in one quarrel and practise the golden rule each day this week.

intro: Theme: “He believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness.”
An honest complaint, a sky full of stars, a covenant God signs alone, and the fruit by which true faith is known.

sub: Do not be afraid, I am your shield.
q: He brought him outside and said, “Look toward heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your descendants be.”
Therefore from one person, and this one as good as dead, descendants were born, “as many as the stars of heaven and as the innumerable grains of sand by the seashore.”
points.apply: Bring God one honest disappointment in prayer today, and end with Abram's act of faith: I believe.

sub: The pieces and the birds of prey.
q: He is mindful of his covenant forever, of the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
For what does the scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.”
points.apply: At the consecration this week, thank God that his covenant with you rests on his faithfulness, not on your strength.

points.h: You will know them by their fruits
sub: Grapes are not gathered from thorns.
The true prophet points to Christ.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
points.apply: Test one religious message you receive this week by its fruit before you believe it or share it.

concl: Abram believed God's promise under the stars, and God bound himself to Abram in a covenant he alone sealed.
True faith bears good fruit; tomorrow's feast shows us John the Baptist, the true prophet who pointed to Christ.
2027-06-23.resolve: Make an act of faith each night this week, and ask God to show you one fruit of his Spirit to grow in.

intro: Theme: “His name is John.”
Called from the womb, wonderfully made, named for God's grace, and glad to decrease so that Christ may increase.

sub: The Servant named in the womb.
Filled with the Spirit before birth.
q: The Lord called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly today, thanking God who called you by name.

sub: The child who leapt for joy.
The dignity of every unborn child.
q: For it was you who formed my inward parts; you knit me together in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
For as soon as I heard the sound of your greeting, the child in my womb leaped for joy.
points.apply: Support a mother in difficulty or a pro-life work this month with prayer, time or help.

q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me,
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And all of them were amazed.
points.apply: Pray the Benedictus each morning this week, and let God open your mouth in praise.

sub: Not worthy to untie his sandals.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: In one conversation this week, speak of Christ rather than of yourself.

concl: John was called and filled with the Spirit before his birth, and named by God for his grace.
The greatest of the prophets found his greatness in pointing to Christ: he must increase, but I must decrease.
2027-06-24.resolve: Thank God for the gift of life each day this week and point someone to Christ.

intro: Theme: “I do choose. Be made clean!”
A new name for Abraham, a laugh turned to joy, and the hand of Jesus that touches the untouchable.

points.h: A new name, a new mission
sub: God Almighty, the God who is enough.
Abram becomes Abraham, Sarai becomes Sarah.
A covenant carried in body and family.
q: No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you the ancestor of a multitude of nations.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.
points.apply: Remember your baptismal name this week and the saint who bears it; ask what mission God gave you with that name.

q: Then Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?”
No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, being fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.
points.apply: Bring to God in prayer one hope you have given up on, and thank him in advance for his faithfulness.

q: He shall remain unclean as long as he has the disease; he is unclean. He shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I do choose. Be made clean!” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
points.apply: This week go to confession and let the Lord say to you: I do choose. Be made clean.

concl: God renews his covenant with Abraham and promises the impossible son, turning the laugh of doubt into the laugh of joy.
Jesus touches the leper whom the world kept at a distance, and shows the heart of God who wants to make us clean.
2027-06-25.resolve: Each day this week reach out to one person whom others leave alone.

intro: Theme: “Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?”
Hospitality at Mamre, a promise that makes Sarah laugh and Mary sing, and a soldier whose faith amazes Jesus.

q: He said, “My lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant. Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: This week offer simple hospitality to someone who is not family: a meal, a cup of tea, a place to rest.

points.h: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
q: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord? At the set time I will return to you, in due season, and Sarah shall have a son.
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Write down the situation you find most impossible, and pray over it each evening this week with the Magnificat.

sub: Many will come from east and west.
q: He sent out his word and healed them, and delivered them from destruction.
The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only speak the word, and my servant will be healed.
points.apply: Before each Communion this week, name silently one person you bring to the Lord with the centurion's words.

concl: At Mamre God comes as a guest and asks Sarah, and us, whether anything is too wonderful for him.
Mary's faith and the centurion's faith show the answer: God's word is enough, and his table is open to all nations.
2027-06-26.resolve: Welcome one guest this week as if Christ himself had come to your door.

intro: Theme: “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?”
Abraham's bold intercession, the cost of following Jesus, and St Irenaeus, who stood for the faith of the apostles.

sub: God shares his plan with a friend.
q: Abraham answered, “Let me take it upon myself to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes.
First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone,
points.apply: Each evening this week, before your own needs, pray for one town, one family and one person far from God.

sub: God more ready to forgive than we are to ask.
q: Then he said, “Oh do not let the Lord be angry if I speak just once more. Suppose ten are found there.” He answered, “For the sake of ten I will not destroy it.”
For just as by the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners, so by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous.
points.apply: Be one of the righteous in your street: do one act of honesty or kindness each day this week that no one asks of you.

sub: Let the dead bury their own dead.
St Irenaeus leaves all to guard the faith.
q: He left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.”
And Jesus said to him, “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
points.apply: Do this week the one thing you have been postponing that Jesus is clearly asking of you.

concl: Abraham shows that God wants friends who stand before him for others, and that he is more ready to forgive than we are to ask.
Jesus asks disciples who will follow him first of all, like St Irenaeus, who left his homeland and gave his life to keep the faith of the apostles.
2027-06-28.resolve: Pray each day this week for your town or village, and do without delay what Jesus asks of you.

intro: Theme: “God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.”
The God who hears the outcast and opens our eyes, and the Lord whom some send away and the martyrs would not let go.

q: And God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
points.apply: Tell God honestly this week the fear you have been carrying alone, and let someone you trust help you carry it.

sub: God with the boy as he grew.
q: Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. She went, and filled the skin with water, and gave the boy a drink.
but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.
points.apply: Each night this week name one help God gave you that day which you did not notice at first.

sub: The martyrs who would not let him go.
q: This poor soul cried, and was heard by the Lord, and was saved from every trouble.
Then the whole town came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their neighborhood.
points.apply: Give Jesus this week the one area of your life you have been keeping closed to him.

concl: God hears the cry of the outcast and opens Hagar's eyes to the well that was already there.
Some ask Jesus to leave because they fear their losses; the first martyrs of Rome lost everything rather than lose him.
2027-06-30.resolve: This week listen for one cry you have been ignoring, and answer it in Jesus' name.
